chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr al-Nakha'i, from Shihab ibn 'Abd Rabbih, or from a man from Shihab, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He asked me, and said to me: 'O Shihab, how many times have you performed Hajj?' I said: 'Nineteen.' He said to me: 'Complete it to twenty times, and Allah will write for you the reward of one Ziyarat (pilgrimation/visitation) of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.زِيَارَةَ: Visitation/Pilgrimage (specifically to the shrine of an Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Hajj twenty times according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) tells Shihab that completing twenty Hajj pilgries grants the reward of one Ziyarat of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), linking the ritual of Hajj to the spiritual station of the Ahl al-Bayt. This comparison underscores the immense virtue of visiting the Imam’s shrine, suggesting that the devotion required for Hajj is mirrored in the reverence shown to the Ahl al-Bayt. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that Ziyarat is not merely a visit but a profound act of worship with equivalent spiritual weight.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 36. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. al-Hussain from Ahmad b. al-Nadhr Nakha’i from Shihab b. Abd Rabbuhu or from a man from Shihab from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
“Perform it twenty times and you would be like one who does the Ziyarat of Imam Husain Ibne Ali (a.s.) once.”
